# Ligand effects in a defined catalyst-A window

## Abstract

Under the reported catalyst-A and substrate conditions, ligand L1 was associated with higher isolated yield than the listed comparators. This observation is limited to the tested substrate class, temperature, solvent, reaction time, and work-up. A negative result with a hindered substrate and a study using a different endpoint show why the evidence does not support a universal ligand ranking. The role of catalyst speciation remains a hypothesis for future testing.

## Evidence-bounded comparison

The primary study reported an increase in isolated yield from 42% to 78% for the stated substrate and conditions [1, p. 2, Table 1]. An independent study observed a similar local association, while another substrate showed little difference [2, p. 3, Figure 2; 3, p. 4, Table 2]. These results support a condition-bound comparison rather than a general rule.

The unidentified by-product in the hindered-substrate experiment was not structurally assigned [4, p. 5, Table 3]. Docking scores and isolated yields measure different endpoints and therefore cannot be ranked together. The current review does not establish behavior across other catalyst states; that question requires additional primary evidence.

| Study | Endpoint | Scope and limitation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| F-001 | isolated yield with substrate denominator | one substrate class; catalyst-A window |
| F-002 | docking score | not directly comparable with isolated yield |

Figure 1. Source-linked scheme from the primary study [1, p. 2, Figure 1].

## Conclusion

The evidence supports a local association between L1 and isolated yield under the tested conditions. Whether this reflects catalyst speciation, substrate effects, or another factor remains unresolved. A controlled substrate-and-catalyst panel with a common endpoint and denominator would be the most useful next test.
